conversion_pathway.process: Form-dependent folate processing and folate-cycle conversion supply 5-methyltetrahydrofolate; folic acid requires reduction.
conversion_pathway.limitations: This conversion pathway does not show that increasing folate intake increases tissue remethylation flux. Folic acid lowers blood homocysteine, which is a circulating marker. The primary source is a biochemical review, not a new human flux study. Reaction identity does not show that ordinary dietary intake controls tissue remethylation rate, and it does not assign clinical benefit. Phosphatidylethanolamine methylation is a later SAMe-consuming reaction, not part of this step.

Folic acid lowers blood homocysteine, which is a circulating marker. The primary source is a biochemical review, not a new human flux study. Reaction identity does not show that ordinary dietary intake controls tissue remethylation rate, and it does not assign clinical benefit. Phosphatidylethanolamine methylation is a later SAMe-consuming reaction, not part of this step.

conversion_pathway.limitations: Provision of vitamin B12 does not show that increasing intake raises tissue remethylation flux. Added vitamin B12 further lowered blood homocysteine beyond folic acid in pooled trials, which remains a circulating marker. The primary source is a biochemical review, not a new human flux study. Reaction identity does not show that ordinary dietary intake controls tissue remethylation rate, and it does not assign clinical benefit. Phosphatidylethanolamine methylation is a later SAMe-consuming reaction, not part of this step.

food_evidence.limitations: Zeisel et al. (2003) Table 1, corrected by the erratum, reports 129 mg betaine per 100 g in raw beets. Canned beets in that table are 334 mg per 100 g. USDA Release 2 reports 130 mg per 100 g for the same raw NDB.

limitations: Supplemental betaine lowers plasma homocysteine in healthy adults, but that change does not measure tissue BHMT activity or show a clinical benefit. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved.

conversion_pathway.process: Choline oxidation supplies betaine upstream of BHMT.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved. Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. The enzyme evidence uses purified or recombinant human protein, not intact human metabolism. Loss of activity after removing zinc ligands does not show that dietary zinc usually limits the enzyme. The review statement that the pathway is independent of folate and vitamin B12 is not a new flux experiment. Quantitative claims in that review about choline deficiency and liver methionine were not re-checked in the primary animal papers. Purified, stable human choline dehydrogenase has been difficult to obtain, so some catalytic detail is inferred from related enzymes and from tissue activity rather than from a complete human kinetic characterisation. The reviews do not show that raising choline intake increases BHMT flux in people.

conversion_pathway.limitations: Dietary protein supplies methionine. It does not show that eating more protein increases cycle rates. DIAAS scores sulfur amino acids as methionine plus cysteine. food_evidence.evidence: Validated UHPLC measured native phosphorylated vitamers separately from unphosphorylated vitamers in commercial cow milk (Schmidt et al., 2017).
food_evidence.limitations: Verified qualitative vitamer occurrence. No individual amount is inferred from total vitamin B6 or B2. Preparation-specific concentrations are not transcribed. Food occurrence does not demonstrate intact cofactor delivery to the receiving tissue.

limitations: Purified-enzyme dependence on pyridoxal 5'-phosphate does not show that raising vitamin B6 intake increases cysteine formation in people. Moderate B6 restriction changed cystathionine handling but did not significantly reduce total transsulfuration in the assessed human tracer study.

conversion_pathway.process: Vitamer-specific endogenous activation; alternative ordered routes, not one chemical reaction
dependencies: PNPO and FMN for PNP/PMP routes

evidence.statement: Human PDXK and PNPO enzymology supports distinct substrate-specific activation routes to the same canonical PLP target.

dependencies: ATP–divalent-metal substrate complex; metal effects depend on assay context
steps.limitations: PN and PM phosphorylation produces PNP and PMP, not PLP directly. In-vitro metal efficacy does not establish a dietary zinc requirement.

limitations: Cysteine is the substrate of the first assembly step. A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, and that formula also removed methionine. When methionine intake stayed adequate, removing cysteine did not lower red-cell synthesis in young men. This does not show that eating more cysteine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis.

conversion_pathway.process: Methionine can supply cysteine through upstream transsulfuration before glutathione assembly.
conversion_pathway.limitations: A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, so that result does not isolate methionine. In the cysteine-free study, methionine intake stayed adequate and red-cell synthesis did not fall. This does not show that eating more methionine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis. All three studies measured blood-cell, not neuronal, synthesis. The sulfur-amino-acid-free diet was an experimental amino-acid formula in seven young men for 10 days. The older-adult increase required combined supplementation and was not an isolated N-acetylcysteine or glycine test, not an ADHD trial, and not ordinary food. The cysteine-free arm used only four young men and two days of adaptation. Concentration did not track synthesis rate in the sulfur-amino-acid-free study.

relationships.operation: Recycle homocysteine to methionine through folate and B12 so methyl-donor supply and homocysteine control stay supported.
relationships.biological_role: Methyl-group donor substrate for methionine synthase. The enzyme transfers that methyl group to homocysteine and releases tetrahydrofolate.
relationships.dietary_input_note: Foods directly supply preformed 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, including polyglutamated forms deconjugated during intestinal absorption. Other dietary folate forms can supply this target through folate metabolism and MTHFR-dependent conversion. Form-specific presence is supported; total folate values must not be relabelled as 5-MTHF quantities or added to 5-MTHF as a separate independent nutrient supply.
relationships.limitation: Necessity of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate does not show that raising its intake increases tissue methionine-synthase flux.
relationships.qualification: Foods directly supply preformed 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, including polyglutamated forms deconjugated during intestinal absorption. conversion_pathway.process: Form-dependent folate processing and folate-cycle conversion supply 5-methyltetrahydrofolate; folic acid requires reduction.
conversion_pathway.limitations: This conversion pathway does not show that increasing folate intake increases tissue remethylation flux. Folic acid lowers blood homocysteine, which is a circulating marker. The primary source is a biochemical review, not a new human flux study. Reaction identity does not show that ordinary dietary intake controls tissue remethylation rate, and it does not assign clinical benefit. Phosphatidylethanolamine methylation is a later SAMe-consuming reaction, not part of this step.

relationships.operation: Provide a parallel homocysteine clearance route so methionine and SAMe supply remain resilient when folate demand is high.
relationships.biological_role: Methyl-donor substrate for BHMT remethylation of homocysteine to methionine
relationships.dietary_input_note: Dietary applicability is already admitted in the Direct/Derived section. This does not establish ordinary-food equivalence, a quantitative requirement, extra-intake benefit or independent supply of a derived product.
relationships.limitation: Supplemental betaine lowers plasma homocysteine in healthy adults, but that change does not measure tissue BHMT activity or show a clinical benefit. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved.

conversion_pathway.process: Choline oxidation supplies betaine upstream of BHMT.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved. Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. The enzyme evidence uses purified or recombinant human protein, not intact human metabolism. Loss of activity after removing zinc ligands does not show that dietary zinc usually limits the enzyme. The review statement that the pathway is independent of folate and vitamin B12 is not a new flux experiment. Quantitative claims in that review about choline deficiency and liver methionine were not re-checked in the primary animal papers. Purified, stable human choline dehydrogenase has been difficult to obtain, so some catalytic detail is inferred from related enzymes and from tissue activity rather than from a complete human kinetic characterisation. The reviews do not show that raising choline intake increases BHMT flux in people.

relationships.dietary_input_note: Accepted upstream dietary constituent provision is distinct from the pool/constraint reference. Existing role, conditional scope and limitations remain unchanged.
relationships.limitation: BHMT activity is concentrated mainly in liver and kidney; this is not local BHMT activity in every tissue. Folate-dependent remethylation and dietary methionine provide alternative supply. Homocysteine lowering does not establish increased MAT flux, increased SAMe availability or benefit from extra intake in replete individuals.
relationships.qualification: Accepted upstream dietary constituent provision is distinct from the pool/constraint reference. Existing role, conditional scope and limitations remain unchanged. Supported upstream resource supply; not reclassified as limiting iKC applicability.

functional_dependency.statement: Dietary methionine can supply cysteine for glutathione assembly. Methionine is not a substrate of the assembly enzymes.

dietary_supply.statement: Dietary methionine can supply cysteine for glutathione assembly. Methionine is not a substrate of the assembly enzymes.

conversion_pathway.process: Methionine can supply cysteine through upstream transsulfuration before glutathione assembly.
conversion_pathway.limitations: A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, so that result does not isolate methionine. In the cysteine-free study, methionine intake stayed adequate and red-cell synthesis did not fall. This does not show that eating more methionine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis. All three studies measured blood-cell, not neuronal, synthesis. The sulfur-amino-acid-free diet was an experimental amino-acid formula in seven young men for 10 days. The older-adult increase required combined supplementation and was not an isolated N-acetylcysteine or glycine test, not an ADHD trial, and not ordinary food. The cysteine-free arm used only four young men and two days of adaptation. Concentration did not track synthesis rate in the sulfur-amino-acid-free study.

observations.label: 5-Methyltetrahydrofolate
observations.evidence_material: Raw vegetable, analytical sample treated for folate extraction
observations.chemical_form: 5-MTHF equivalents, summed monoglutamate and polyglutamate species
observations.source_reference: Wang, Riedl and Schwartz (2010), Journal of Chromatography B 878(29), 2949–2958, Table 5
observations.source_note: Calculated from the reported Table 5 molar sum, not directly reported mass concentration. Includes polyglutamate species as monoglutamate equivalents, not their intact molecular masses. Glu8 response was estimated by calibration extrapolation; this sample includes that estimated component. Analytical steaming was extraction treatment, not a cooked-food state. One study sample does not establish universal food composition; do not add this vitamer value to total folate as an independent nutrient supply.
